question: In which of the following years the East India Company introduced the Permanent Settlement?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1793**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Permanent Settlement** was introduced by the **East India Company** in the year **1793** during the tenure of **Lord Cornwallis**, the Governor-General of India.
 
• It was primarily implemented in the regions of **Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha**, and later extended to the northern parts of Madras and Varanasi.
 
• The settlement was designed to establish a fixed revenue system where landlords or **Zamindars** were made responsible for paying a fixed amount of land revenue to the British government.
 
• Under this system, the revenue amount was **permanently fixed**, meaning it would not change regardless of variations in agricultural production or economic conditions.
 
• The Zamindars were given hereditary rights to collect revenue from the peasants, turning them into intermediaries between the British government and the cultivators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of the Permanent Settlement:**

 
 
• To ensure a **stable revenue** system for the East India Company by fixing the revenue permanently.
 
• To create a class of landlords or **Zamindars** who would be loyal to the British government and act as collaborators.
 
• To promote agricultural productivity by encouraging Zamindars to invest in land improvements, as they would retain the profits.
 
 
 
• **Features of the Permanent Settlement:**
 
 
• The revenue rates were fixed **permanently**, irrespective of economic changes or fluctuations in agricultural output.
 
• The Zamindars were given **hereditary rights** over the land and could pass their ownership to their descendants.
 
• If the Zamindars failed to pay the fixed revenue, their lands could be confiscated and auctioned by the government.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Permanent Settlement:**
 
 
• It led to the emergence of a class of wealthy Zamindars, but many of them exploited the peasants through high rents and forced labor.
 
• The system discouraged agricultural innovation, as Zamindars focused more on maximizing revenue collection than improving land productivity.
 
• Peasants were often subjected to economic hardships, as they bore the brunt of fixed revenue demands even during periods of crop failure or natural calamities.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Revenue Systems:**
 
 
• Unlike the **Ryotwari system**, where farmers directly paid revenue to the government, the Permanent Settlement created intermediaries like Zamindars.
 
• The **Mahalwari system**, implemented in northern India, involved village communities collectively paying revenue, which was periodically revised, unlike the fixed nature of the Permanent Settlement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lord Cornwallis:**

 
 
• He served as the **Governor-General of India** from **1786 to 1793**.
 
• He is known for introducing administrative reforms, including the **Permanent Settlement**, and strengthening the judicial system in British India.
 
 
 
• **Regions Covered:**
 
 
• The Permanent Settlement was initially implemented in **Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha** and later extended to other parts of India.
 
 
 
• **Criticism:**
 
 
• The system was criticized for its adverse impact on **peasants**, who faced exploitation and suffered during poor harvests.
 
• It failed to achieve its objective of improving agricultural productivity, as Zamindars prioritized revenue collection over land development.
